original_value: Task oriented dialog agents provide a natural language interface for users to complete their goal. Dialog State Tracking (DST), which is often a core component of these systems, tracks the system's understanding of the user's goal throughout the conversation. To enable accurate multi-domain DST, the model needs to encode dependencies between past utterances and slot semantics and understand the dialog context, including long-range cross-domain references. We introduce a novel architecture for this task to encode the conversation history and slot semantics more robustly by using attention mechanisms at multiple granularities. In particular, we use cross-attention to model relationships between the context and slots at different semantic levels and self-attention to resolve cross-domain coreferences. In addition, our proposed architecture does not rely on knowing the domain ontologies beforehand and can also be used in a zero-shot setting for new domains or unseen slot values. Our model improves the joint goal accuracy by 5% (absolute) in the full-data setting and by up to 2% (absolute) in the zero-shot setting over the present state-of-the-art on the MultiWoZ 2.1 dataset.

result.paraphrase: Task-oriented dialogue agents give users a natural-language way to accomplish their goals. Dialog State Tracking (DST), often a central part of such systems, monitors the system’s interpretation of the user’s goal over the course of the conversation. For accurate multi-domain DST, the model must capture dependencies between prior utterances and slot semantics while understanding dialog context, including long-range cross-domain references. We present a new architecture for this task that more robustly encodes conversation history and slot semantics with attention mechanisms at multiple levels of granularity. Specifically, cross-attention models relations between context and slots at different semantic levels, and self-attention resolves cross-domain coreference. The proposed architecture also does not require prior knowledge of domain ontologies and can operate in a zero-shot setting for new domains or unseen slot values. On the MultiWoZ 2.1 dataset, our model improves joint goal accuracy by 5% absolute in the full-data setting and by up to 2% absolute in the zero-shot setting over the current state of the art.
